title: Fair Vaccine Sharing Could Save Millions in Future Pandemics
subtitle: A new report suggests that changing how we distribute medicine globally could prevent millions of deaths.

summary.en: A new study reveals that sharing vaccines based on population size rather than wealth could save 2.7 million lives during a future pandemic. Researchers from the NUS-Lancet Prime commission argue that current systems are too focused on rich nations. The report highlights that social inequality makes it harder for vulnerable groups to stay safe. Experts call for better community involvement and stronger local manufacturing to prepare for health crises. Governments are urged to change their planning before the next global outbreak occurs.
summary.zh: 一項最新研究顯示，若能根據人口規模而非財力分配疫苗，未來若發生大流行病，將能拯救兩百七十萬人的性命。新加坡國立大學與刺胳針委員會的研究人員主張，現行制度過於偏袒富裕國家。報告強調，社會不平等使得弱勢群體更難獲得保障。專家呼籲加強社區參與並提升在地製造能力，以應對健康危機。各國政府受促在下一次全球疫情爆發前，調整其應對規劃。

paragraphs.en: A new study has revealed that the world could save nearly 3 million additional lives during a future pandemic if countries change how they share vaccines. According to The Guardian Health, researchers looked at a possible future flu outbreak to understand how different ways of distributing medicine affect global survival rates. The study found that while fast development of vaccines is important, the way they are shared is just as critical for saving lives.
paragraphs.zh: 一項最新研究顯示，若各國能改變疫苗分配方式，未來若發生大流行病，全球將能多拯救近三百萬人的性命。根據《衛報健康》（The Guardian Health）報導，研究人員針對未來可能爆發的流感進行分析，以了解不同的藥物分配方式如何影響全球存活率。研究發現，雖然快速研發疫苗至關重要，但疫苗的分配方式對於挽救生命同樣關鍵。

paragraphs.en: Currently, many countries buy vaccines based on their wealth, which often leaves poorer nations waiting at the back of the line. The NUS-Lancet Prime commission, which published the report, suggests that if vaccines were distributed based on population size instead of purchasing power, the world would see a significant drop in total deaths. The Guardian Health reports that this approach could save 2.7 million more people than the current system.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，許多國家根據自身財力購買疫苗，這往往導致較貧窮的國家排在隊伍末端。發布此報告的「新加坡國立大學與刺胳針委員會」（NUS-Lancet Prime commission）建議，若疫苗能根據人口規模而非購買力進行分配，全球死亡總數將顯著下降。《衛報健康》指出，這種做法比起現行制度，能多拯救兩百七十萬人。

paragraphs.en: However, this change comes with a difficult trade-off. The modelling shows that if richer countries shared their supply more fairly, their own death tolls might rise. In high-income nations, deaths could increase from 2.4 million to 3.9 million under this fairer system. Despite this, the commission argues that global cooperation is necessary to stop a pandemic from spreading uncontrollably.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，這項改變伴隨著艱難的取捨。模型顯示，若富裕國家更公平地分享疫苗供應，其國內的死亡人數可能會上升。在這種更公平的制度下，高收入國家的死亡人數可能從兩百四十萬增加至三百九十萬。儘管如此，委員會主張，全球合作對於遏止大流行病失控擴散是必要的。

paragraphs.en: Helen Clark, a former prime minister of New Zealand and a leader of the commission, explained that solidarity—the act of standing together and helping others—is essential. She noted that protecting health workers and people in need everywhere helps stop the virus from spreading. The commission also found that increasing public confidence in vaccines could save an additional 1.9 million lives. This suggests that governments must work harder to earn the trust of their people before a crisis begins.
paragraphs.zh: 紐西蘭前總理、同時也是委員會領導人之一的克拉克（Helen Clark）解釋說，團結一致、互相扶持的精神至關重要。她指出，保護各地的醫護人員與弱勢族群，有助於阻止病毒傳播。委員會還發現，提升大眾對疫苗的信心能額外拯救一百九十萬人的性命。這顯示政府必須在危機發生前，更努力贏得民眾的信任。

paragraphs.en: The report is the result of research conducted in 20 different countries. Experts spoke with people who were hit hard by previous health crises, including homeless individuals in Indonesia and families in the UK who lost loved ones to Covid-19. Professor Helena Legido-Quigley of Imperial College London, a co-chair of the commission, explained that many people are at higher risk simply because of their living conditions. She pointed out that a person living in a crowded home cannot easily stay away from others, and someone without official identity papers may not be able to get government help or health services.
paragraphs.zh: 這份報告是針對二十個不同國家進行研究的成果。專家訪談了曾受過往健康危機嚴重衝擊的民眾，包括印尼的無家可歸者，以及英國失去親人的家庭。委員會共同主席、倫敦帝國學院（Imperial College London）的雷吉多-奎格利教授（Helena Legido-Quigley）解釋說，許多人僅因生活條件而面臨更高風險。她指出，居住在擁擠環境中的人難以與他人保持距離，而沒有正式身分證明文件的人，可能無法獲得政府援助或醫療服務。

paragraphs.en: Many traditional plans for pandemics focus only on technical things, like having enough hospital beds or medical equipment. The researchers argue that these plans often fail because they do not consider the real lives of ordinary people. Dr. Githinji Gitahi, the global CEO of Amref Health Africa, told The Guardian Health that plans made in offices in big cities often ignore the reality of people on the ground. He noted that countries in Africa were at the back of the queue for Covid-19 vaccines, and he described the new findings as both "compelling and deeply sobering."
paragraphs.zh: 許多傳統的大流行病應對計畫僅聚焦於技術層面，例如確保醫院病床或醫療設備充足。研究人員認為，這些計畫往往因為忽略了普通民眾的真實生活而失敗。非洲醫療與研究基金會（Amref Health Africa）全球執行長吉塔希博士（Dr. Githinji Gitahi）向《衛報健康》表示，在大城市辦公室裡制定的計畫，往往無視基層民眾的現實處境。他提到，非洲國家在新冠肺炎（Covid-19）疫苗分配上處於劣勢，並形容這些新發現既「令人信服且發人深省」。

paragraphs.en: To fix these problems, the commission has created a new plan for action. They are calling on governments to include local communities in their planning processes. Instead of just relying on checklists, leaders should make sure that health systems are designed to listen to the people they serve. This means building better research and manufacturing capacity in different regions so that vaccines can be produced and delivered faster when they are needed most.
paragraphs.zh: 為了修正這些問題，委員會制定了一項新的行動計畫。他們呼籲各國政府將在地社區納入規劃流程。領導者不應僅依賴檢查清單，而應確保醫療體系設計能傾聽服務對象的心聲。這意味著要在不同地區建立更好的研究與製造能力，以便在最需要時能更快生產並運送疫苗。

paragraphs.en: The findings are being presented ahead of a United Nations meeting on pandemic preparedness in New York. The message from the experts is clear: trust cannot be built once a crisis has already started. It must be earned now, through health systems that are fair, inclusive, and ready to protect everyone, not just those in the wealthiest countries. By working together and focusing on the most vulnerable, the world can be much better prepared for the next time a global health threat appears.
paragraphs.zh: 這些研究結果將在紐約舉行的聯合國大流行病防範會議前提出。專家們傳達的訊息很明確：信任無法在危機爆發後才建立。必須從現在開始，透過公平、包容且準備好保護所有人的醫療體系來贏得信任，而不僅僅是保護最富裕國家的民眾。透過共同努力並關注最脆弱的群體，全球將能為下一次全球健康威脅的出現做好更充分的準備。

keyTerms.definitionEn: A row of people or things waiting for something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 在文中指排隊順序，容易與「線條」的常見意思混淆。文中：Currently, many countries buy vaccines based on their wealth, which often leaves poorer nations waiting at the back of the line.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A situation where you must accept the loss of one thing in return for gaining another.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 權衡、取捨（為了得到某物而必須放棄另一物）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞片語 trade off 演變而來的名詞，常指兩難的抉擇。文中：However, this change comes with a difficult trade-off.

keyTerms.definitionEn: In the real, practical situation, rather than in theory or from a distance.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 在實地、在第一線（指實際生活狀況）。
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思是「在地上」，這裡指實際現場的狀況。文中：Dr. Githinji Gitahi, the global CEO of Amref Health Africa, told The Guardian Health that plans made in offices in big cities often ignore the reality of people on the ground.

keyTerms.definitionEn: A line of people or vehicles waiting for something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 與前文的 line 同義，在英式英語中較常用，對於習慣美式英語的學習者來說較陌生。文中：He noted that countries in Africa were at the back of the queue for Covid-19 vaccines, and he described the new findings as both "compelling and deeply sobering."

sources.name: The Guardian Health
sources.title: Nearly 3m more lives could be saved in next pandemic if vaccines are shared more fairly, says report

quiz.question: According to the report, what is one specific condition that increases a person's risk during a health crisis?

options.A: Living in a large city with many hospitals.
options.C: Having a high income but no access to vaccines.
options.D: Being a healthcare worker in a rural area.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第五段，Professor Helena Legido-Quigley 指出，沒有官方身分證件的人可能無法獲得政府援助或醫療服務，這增加了他們的風險。選項 A 與文中提到的「住在擁擠的家中」相反；選項 C 文中未提及；選項 D 雖然提到醫護人員，但文章強調的是保護他們，而非他們因處於鄉村而處於高風險。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between vaccine distribution and national wealth?

options.A: Richer countries are currently less affected by pandemics because they manufacture all their own vaccines.
options.B: Changing the distribution system to favor population size would likely result in more deaths in wealthy nations.
options.C: Poorer nations have refused to participate in global vaccine sharing programs in the past.
options.D: The current system of vaccine distribution is designed to prioritize the most vulnerable populations.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第三段指出，如果富裕國家更公平地分享疫苗，他們自身的死亡人數可能會從 240 萬增加到 390 萬，這暗示了改變現行體系會對富國造成代價。選項 A 文中未提及富國製造所有疫苗；選項 C 文中並未提到貧窮國家拒絕合作；選項 D 顯然錯誤，因為目前的系統是基於購買力而非人口或脆弱性。

quiz.question: In the sixth paragraph, what does Dr. Githinji Gitahi mean when he describes the findings as 'sobering'?

options.A: The findings are confusing and difficult to understand.
options.B: The findings are surprising and make people feel very happy.
options.C: The findings are serious and make people think carefully about the reality.
options.D: The findings are boring and lack practical importance.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。在上下文語境中，「sobering」形容那些讓人冷靜、嚴肅思考的現實，通常指令人警醒的訊息。選項 A 與困惑無關；選項 B 與「sobering」的負面嚴肅感相反；選項 D 錯誤，因為研究結果被認為具有重要性，而非無聊。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding future pandemic preparedness?

options.A: Governments should focus primarily on building more hospitals and buying medical equipment.
options.B: The most effective way to stop a pandemic is to prioritize vaccine sales to the highest bidder.
options.C: Global cooperation, inclusive planning, and building trust are essential for saving lives.
options.D: Individual actions, like staying home, are more important than how governments distribute vaccines.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章的核心在於強調公平分配疫苗、建立公眾信任以及將社區需求納入規劃的重要性，這些都是為了全球合作以應對大流行。選項 A 是文章中提到「傳統計畫」的不足之處；選項 B 與文章主旨背道而馳；選項 D 雖然提到個人行為，但文章重心在於政府政策與全球系統性的改革。
